Naomi / Jordan — thanks for the tag. I reviewed HelixCloud's redlines and attached EvidenceChecklist. Below are suggested positions that balance risk and commercial reality.

Key legal compromises we can offer (draft language below):
1) Scope narrowing: Redwood will indemnify HelixCloud for third-party claims that the Redwood Service (defined as the hosted inference endpoints and model outputs as generated by the service) infringes a third party's U.S. or E.U. patents, copyrights, or trademark rights, but only to the extent the claim arises solely from Redwood's models or model-serving code. The indemnity excludes: (a) Customer Content; (b) content derived from Customer-provided data; (c) upstream open-source dependencies identified in Appendix A; and (d) claims based on modifications made by HelixCloud.

2) Defense control / settlement: Redwood will have the right to assume defense with counsel of its choice, subject to HelixCloud's reasonable consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) when the claim includes an allegation unrelated to Redwood's Service. Redwood will not be obligated to pay settlements that include non-monetary obligations without Redwood's prior written consent.

3) Financial cap & insurance-offset: propose the Order Form cap applies to IP indemnity (i.e., the lesser of the Order Form cap and $3,000,000 per claim). Regarding insurance-offset, we will accept an offset against indemnity damages only after HelixCloud has exhausted proceeds available under HelixCloud's primary insurer(s) for the relevant loss and only to the extent such proceeds are actually received by HelixCloud. We do not accept an immediate dollar-for-dollar offset at the time of claim notification.

4) Evidence and preservation: HelixCloud must preserve logs, provide the EvidenceChecklist items, and provide access to reasonable samples and reproduction steps. Redwood may decline indemnity if HelixCloud fails to timely preserve or provide the requested evidence that materially prejudices our ability to defend.

Rationale: this keeps exposure bounded (model-output-limited + order-form cap), preserves Redwood's ability to control defense strategy, and prevents premature offsets that could leave Redwood paying defense costs while Helix obtains insurance proceeds.

Draft paragraph (redline-ready):
"Redwood shall indemnify and hold harmless Buyer from and against any Losses arising out of any third-party claim that the Redwood Service, as delivered and operated by Redwood, infringes such third party's intellectual property rights, provided that (i) such claim arises solely from the use of Redwood's models or model-serving software, and (ii) Buyer promptly provides Redwood written notice and the evidence set forth in Exhibit D. Redwood's liability under this Section shall be subject to the Order Form cap (and in no event exceed $3,000,000 per claim). Any amounts payable under this Section will be reduced by proceeds actually received by Buyer from Buyer's primary insurer(s) for the relevant Losses, but only after such proceeds have been exhausted and actually collected by Buyer."

Next steps: I recommend we send this as a counter and ask Helix to identify any specific upstream dependency they want carved out in Appendix A. Also, ask procurement for sample insurance declarations if they plan to assert an offset.

-Kim

Naomi / Kim — thanks for the quick review. A few points from our side: 

• Scope: HelixCloud cannot accept an indemnity limited only to a narrow "model-output" definition. Our customers run product workflows that mix customer content and model outputs — we need protection for infringement claims that arise from the combined output of the service as they experience it.

• Insurance offset timing: we are not willing to wait until our insurer pays out before deducting proceeds; that creates a substantial timing mismatch that leaves HelixCloud out-of-pocket while pursuing recovery. We want either (i) an immediate setoff against indemnity payments (with a reconciliation after actual insurance recoveries), or (ii) Redwood to agree to a higher cap to balance that timing risk.

• Evidence: we can provide the EvidenceChecklist but will not be able to produce model weights or underlying proprietary telemetry beyond what is strictly necessary for reproducing the issue. Please confirm acceptable minimums.

Our counsel is preparing a response and will share redline comments this week. We are targeting procurement signoff by 2/22 and may escalate to execs if we cannot reach a middle ground.

Regards,
Maria
